title: Chest trouble, rest, post office job and a trumpet studio
summary: After leaving Cab he was hospitalised in Nashville for his chest, rested two years, worked in the post office and taught trumpet, also gigging at the Martinique with Marcelino Guerra.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now you started teaching, you had your own studio here in New York?
This was after I left Cab's band.

I went to Nashville, I stayed -- I was down there in the hospital for about nine -- 10 days, you know, observation I had -- my sister was the superintendent of nurses at the Herbert Hospital in Mahari and naturally she always was interested in me, so she put me in the hospital, I stayed there nine days for observation, you know, chest and all that stuff, which I did have a problem with my chest, which wasn't serious as I thought it was at that time. So I didn't -- the doctors advised me not to -- told me to take a good rest, forget about playing for awhile. So I did, I didn't play for almost two years. So I came back to New York and I -- after I was down there for a while and I worked in the Post Office I was in the Post Office, GPO, went out to the was a postal concentration center for a long time.
And that's when I had a little studio also. I was teaching trumpet at the same time.
Uh-huh. And whom did you teach?

Well, I had quite a lot of kids down there. I don't think I had anybody that you know of. Because at that time the kids that I had about 40 -- 50 students. And they dwindled down to one, but in the meantime I had a little job at the Martinique, with the Marcelino Guerra.
Yes, you got into a whole latin thing.
AT one time and I want to -- want to get into that in a minute.
